headline: Mirza Fakhrul takes oath as 23rd president of Bangladesh
summary: The swearing-in ceremony took place at Bangabhaban, where the new president was administered the oath by Acting Speaker Barrister Kaiser Kamal.
details: Mirza Fakhrul Islam Alamgir has been sworn in as the 23rd President of Bangladesh. The ceremony was held at Bangabhaban, the official residence of the president.
The oath of office was administered by Acting Speaker of Parliament, Barrister Kaiser Kamal.
Following the presidential swearing-in, the new president administered the oath to four new ministers and two state ministers as part of a cabinet reshuffle.
The new cabinet members include figures such as Zahir Uddin Swapon, who was appointed as a Prime Minister's advisor, and Afroza Khanam, who was appointed as the Food Minister.
The reshuffle comes as the government seeks to bring new faces into the Tarique-led cabinet to streamline administration and governance.
caption:
Mirza Fakhrul Islam Alamgir is now the 23rd President of Bangladesh.

Mirza Fakhrul Islam Alamgir has been sworn in as the 23rd President of Bangladesh. The ceremony was held at Bangabhaban, the official residence of the president.

The oath of office was administered by Acting Speaker of Parliament, Barrister Kaiser Kamal.

Following the presidential swearing-in, the new president administered the oath to four new ministers and two state ministers as part of a cabinet reshuffle.

The new cabinet members include figures such as Zahir Uddin Swapon, who was appointed as a Prime Minister's advisor, and Afroza Khanam, who was appointed as the Food Minister.

The reshuffle comes as the government seeks to bring new faces into the Tarique-led cabinet to streamline administration and governance.

headline: 60 kmph winds: Storm warning issued for Dhaka and other districts
summary: Severe weather alerts have been issued for several regions, including the capital, with wind speeds expected to reach 60 km/h.
details: The Meteorological Department has issued a warning for several districts, including Dhaka, regarding the possibility of severe storms tonight.
Wind speeds are expected to reach up to 60 km/h, which could lead to significant disruptions and potential hazards.
Residents in the affected areas are advised to take necessary precautions to secure their homes and avoid staying outdoors during the peak of the storm.
The authorities are monitoring the weather patterns closely to provide real-time updates as the system moves across the region.
